content.text:
1. High: the new rebase path can replay the wrong commit set when the local metadata branch already contains an older merge commit, which can then drop files during cherry-pick. [`push_common.go`](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_common.go#L218) calls `collectCommitsSince`, but that helper only walks `ParentHashes[0]` and never verifies that it actually reached `stopAt` before returning [`push_common.go`](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_common.go#L271). That is unsafe once `entire/checkpoints/v1` has any merge commit from the previous fetch+merge implementation. In that shape, `git merge-base` can legitimately return a commit reachable only through the second parent of the local tip; `collectCommitsSince` will miss it, walk back to root, and replay extra historical commits. `cherryPickOnto` applies both additions and deletions from each replayed commit [`metadata_reconcile.go`](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/metadata_reconcile.go#L285), so an older deletion can remove metadata that still exists on the remote tip. After the next push, that becomes remote data loss, not just a local rewrite.

I do see a real data-loss scenario from rebase because of that first-parent-only traversal. A concrete case is:
1. Repo already has a metadata merge commit from the old sync behavior.
2. Remote advances on the side that is the merge-base through the local tip’s second parent.
3. This code computes the correct merge-base, but `collectCommitsSince` cannot reach it and replays too much history.
4. Any replayed historical deletion wins in `cherryPickOnto`, removing checkpoint files from the rebased branch.

The staged tests do not cover that shape. They only exercise linear divergence and fast-forward cases in [`push_common_test.go`](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_common_test.go), so this regression would slip through.

I ran `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy -run 'TestFetchAndRebase_|TestPushBranchIfNeeded_'`; it passes, but it does not hit the merge-commit ancestry case above.
